context: Single scatter plot mapping prompt word count (x) vs composite output quality score (y) for 105 synthetic blocks, with dot size encoding skill count (1–6) and color encoding 6 skill categories, plus a brush-to-filter interaction, sweet-spot zone annotation, median reference line, and two callout labels.
first_impression: Clean and readable at a glance — the layout is uncluttered, the 6-color palette separates well, and the annotations add interpretive value without overwhelming the data.
what_works: The 6-category palette stays below the color overload threshold and the hues are perceptually distinct enough to match legend entries to dots quickly; the sweet-spot zone and median line together give the viewer two anchors for interpreting position without requiring mental arithmetic.
what_doesnt: The 'Top' callout label renders directly over the subtitle text in the upper-left corner, creating a legibility collision that undermines both; the size channel (skill count 1–6 mapped to radius 3.5–10px) is too compressed to read without hovering, making it a decoration rather than a usable encoding in the dense 40–75 word-count region where overplotting is highest.
